_comment: Curated starting catalog, so Phase 1 is useful with no search API key at all. Everything the team already used successfully is here, plus the obvious platforms around it. `dofollow` is deliberately null almost everywhere — the vetter measures it rather than trusting a list that goes stale. `manualOnly: true` means the platform's terms forbid automated posting: the agent prepares the content and a human posts it.

sites.name: Substack
sites.notes: Already used successfully for blog, profile and a note. Real publication, real readers; the strongest asset in the current profile.

sites.name: JustPaste.it
sites.notes: Publishes without an account. Low authority, but instant and already in use.

sites.name: Pearltrees
sites.notes: Curation platform; collections are public and indexed.

sites.name: Diigo
sites.notes: Used twice already. Public annotations only count if the item is set public.

sites.name: Padlet
sites.notes: Boards are public when shared; doubles as the mindmap target.

sites.name: start.me
sites.notes: Public start pages are indexed. Already in use.

sites.name: Flipboard
sites.notes: Magazines get real traffic. flip.it short links redirect, so the verifier must follow redirects before looking for the link.

sites.name: Buy Me a Coffee
sites.notes: Creator page with a website field. One profile per brand; not a repeatable link source.

sites.name: Reddit
sites.notes: Terms forbid automated posting, and subreddit moderators remove promotional posts fast. Links are nofollow: worth it for traffic and brand, never for link equity. Agent drafts, human posts.

sites.name: Quora
sites.notes: Automated answering is against the terms and gets accounts banned. Nofollow. Manual only.

sites.name: Medium
sites.notes: External links are nofollow and the spam policy targets automated posting. Good for reach, not for authority.

sites.name: Blogger
sites.notes: Free hosted blog on a Google property. A whole blog is an asset, not a one-off submission: set one up properly or not at all.

sites.name: WordPress.com
sites.notes: Marked manual after a real attempt: wordpress.com/ is a marketing page with no submission form, and publishing runs through the Calypso/Gutenberg editor behind a login - a JS app the generic form filler cannot drive. Automating it properly means their REST API with OAuth, which is a project of its own. A human posts it in a minute. Free tier also adds nofollow on some themes; verify per post.

sites.name: Telegraph
sites.notes: No account needed. Indexes inconsistently; cheap to try, never a cornerstone.

sites.name: Write.as
sites.notes: Anonymous publishing; free posts are indexable.

sites.name: Hashnode
sites.notes: Marked manual after a real attempt: hashnode.com/ is a marketing page and the editor sits behind a login in a JS app, exactly like wordpress.com - the generic form filler found no form. Genuinely relevant to an IT training institute, so the content has to be real engineering writing, not keyword filler.

sites.name: DEV Community
sites.notes: Strong fit for the niche but moderators remove thin promotional posts and the terms discourage automation. Human-posted, high-quality articles only.

sites.name: Tumblr
sites.notes: Low effort, low value. Keep for variety in the profile, not for volume.

sites.name: Issuu
sites.notes: Free tier publishes publicly. Links inside a PDF are not crawled as links: the value is the description field and the profile.

sites.name: AnyFlip
sites.notes: Flipbook host. Same caveat: the crawlable link is in the page description, not the document.

sites.name: SlideShare
sites.notes: Still indexed and still gets traffic for how-to decks. Description links are the target.

sites.name: Slides
sites.notes: Public decks on the free plan.

sites.name: Imgur
sites.notes: Nofollow and heavily moderated against promotion. Use for image hosting, not for links.

sites.name: Flickr
sites.notes: Photo pages with a description field; profile carries a website link.

sites.name: Behance
sites.notes: High authority profile link. Needs a genuine portfolio project, so it suits course-project showcases.

sites.name: MindMeister
sites.notes: Free plan allows a few public maps. Mindmap links are the weakest category in the sheet; do not spend real time here.

sites.name: Coggle
sites.notes: Public diagrams get a shareable URL.

sites.name: bubbl.us
sites.notes: Free tier saves a limited number of public maps.

sites.name: Justdial
sites.notes: India's biggest local directory and a real lead source for a Nagpur institute. Listing is phone-verified, so a human completes it once; after that it is a citation to keep consistent, not a repeatable link.

sites.name: Sulekha
sites.notes: Education and training categories are well used in tier-2 cities. Phone verification; human does it once.

sites.name: IndiaMART
sites.notes: B2B oriented; a training institute fits the services side. Verification is manual.

sites.name: Yellow Pages India
sites.notes: Free listing with a website field.

sites.name: TradeIndia
sites.notes: Same shape as IndiaMART.

sites.name: ipt.pw (SEO tools)
sites.rejectReason: Recorded twice in the tracker, but the saved URL was the site's own backlink-maker tool page. Tool pages create no link you own.
sites.notes: Kept in the catalog so it is never re-added as a candidate.

sites.name: Whois.com
sites.rejectReason: A whois lookup page was recorded as a backlink. It is a lookup of your own domain and carries no link you placed.
sites.notes: Blocklisted so it cannot re-enter the catalog.

sites.name: social-bookmarkingsites.com
sites.notes: Generic bookmarking farm — already used once. Let the vetter score it on outbound-link volume rather than assuming.

sites.name: bookmarkrange.com
sites.notes: Same: used once, authority unproven. Vetting decides.
